knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Section 6.3 and table 7: approval covers indoor pools with capacity up to 500,000 litres.
Section 6.3: UV leaves no residual, so hydrogen peroxide is used with UV to provide residual disinfection.
Section 6.3.1 and table 7: peroxide has a floor of 40 mg/L.

practicalCriteria: On a supplied indoor pool, confirms approval, capacity and UV unit status before testing.
Measures hydrogen peroxide, pH plus total alkalinity, and records whether each is in range against the standard.
Escalates a supplied scenario with a shutdown or low peroxide without treating the pool as compliant.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Completed UV system check record for the assessed pool
Shutdown or escalation record in a supplied scenario
Assessor observation of the peroxide test and PPE use
stopWorkCriteria: UV unit not running or in alarm: escalate and keep the pool closed until the operator confirms the unit runs.
Hydrogen peroxide below 40 mg/L: do not treat the pool as compliant; escalate.
Electrical fault in the UV housing: isolate, do not open live equipment, and escalate to a licensed electrician.
